# The Big E Tips For Directions and Parking

Major Home Improvements is excited about the Big E once again this year.

We are big fans of the exposition and visit every single year. After years of visiting we learned a few tips to avoid traffic and find cheap and close parking. Her are a few direction and parking tips for all you New Englanders and New Yorkers.

## Big E Directions & Parking

## General Directions

FROM Connecticut  (Most Used Rout)

Take I-91 North from Route. 2, I-84, I-95 or the Merritt Pkwy. Follow I-91 North to Massachusetts. Take Exit 3 to Route 5 North to Route 147 West (Memorial Avenue) approximately 3/4 miles to Gate 9 parking lot.

Note: Using I-91 north or south to get to the Big E will have the most traffic. We advice you to use alternative routes below to save time and a head-ach.

FROM Worcester/ Boston Are Using Mass-Pike.

Take the Massachusetts Turnpike West to Exit 6 (Springfield). Go left at the light, following I-291 South to I-91 South (right lane) to Exit 3 and follow signs.

OR, take the Massachusetts Turnpike West to Exit 4, to Rte. 5 South to Rte. 147 West. Continue approximately 3/4 mi. to ESE Gate 9 parking lot.

## Avoid Traffic By Using These Routes

Routes from Northern Mass/Vermont using I-91 South.

 Head south on I-91 S
 Take exit Exit 11 for Birnie Ave toward W.Springfield/ US-20 W
 Keep right at the fork, follow signs for MA-20 W/Plainfield St/W. Springfield and merge onto Plainfield St and head towards the 2nd Bridge.
 At the traffic circle, take the 2nd exit onto Park St
 Turn left onto River St
 Turn left onto Memorial Ave

(Note: This area will have traffic and you will need to look for parking around the Gate 9. There are more parking available if you take a Left on Memorial Ave over the bridge.)

Routes from Connecticut using I-91 North.

Route #1

 Head north on I-91 N
 Take exit 47W to merge onto CT-190 W toward Suffield
 Turn right onto CT-159 N/CT-190 W
 Head north on CT-159 N/CT-190 W toward Suffield Meadow Dr (At this point you might want to start looking for parking.)
 Turn right onto MA-147 E/Suffield St towards Gate 9 Big E.

Route #2

 Head north on I-91 N
 Take exit 47W to merge onto CT-190 W toward Suffield
 Turn right onto CT-159 N/CT-190 W
 Turn left onto CT-190 W/Thompsonville Rd
 Turn left onto CT-190 W/Mapleton Ave
 Turn right onto CT-75 N. Head North to Gate 9 Big E

(Once you get close you will see a lot of people walking, this is when you want to start looking for parking.)

Routes from Boston using I-90 West Mass-Pike

Route #1

 Head west on I-90 W
 Take exit 4 for US 5 S/W Springfield
 Merge onto US-5 S/Riverdale St
 Slight right onto the US 20 ramp to West Springfield/Springfield
 At the traffic circle, keep right and exit onto US-20 W/Park St
 Turn left onto River St
 Turn left onto Memorial Ave

(Note: This area will have traffic and you will need to look for parking around the Gate 9. There are more parking available if you take a Left on Mamorial Ave over the bridge.)

Route #2

 Head west on I-90 W
 Take exit 6 for I-291 toward Springfield/Hartford Connecticut
 Use the left 2 lanes to turn left onto I-291 W (signs for Interstate 291 W/Interstate 91/Springfield)
 Take I-291 W to Plainfield St. Take exit 1B-2B from I-291 W
 Turn left onto River St
 Turn left onto Memorial Ave

Routes from Southwestern Connecticut using Route 10/202

Route #1

 Head North on Route. 10/202 towards Granby CT.
 Turn right onto CT-20 E/E Granby Rd
 Turn left onto CT-187 N
 Turn right to stay on CT-187 N
 Turn left to stay on CT-187 N
 Head north on CT-187 N/N Grand St toward Spruce St
 Turn right onto MA-57 E (signs for Massachusetts 57 E/U.S. 5/Interstate 91/Springfield)
 Take the MA-75 exit toward Agawam/W Springfield/Agawam West. Springfield
 Turn left onto MA-75 N/Suffield St (signs for Massachusetts 75 N/W Springfield)
 Continue onto Memorial Ave towards Big E.

Big E Automobile Parking – $10 per vehicle

Automobile parking is available for our guests at Gate 9 for $10 (cash only). Our handicapped parking and drop off area is located inside the Gate 9 parking area at Gate 9A. The Big E provides 580 accessible parking spaces, exceeding the code requirement of 58 spaces, on a first-come, first-served basis. The Gate 9A area is also available for the drop-off/pick-up of handicapped, elderly or otherwise impaired passengers. Several adjacent private parking lots are located in the neighborhoods along Memorial Avenue and are not affiliated with The Big E.

Street/ Residential Parking

If you have never been to Big E. Note that there will be lots of PAID parking available at business parking lots such at the Rockies hardware store and Motel across the street, which usually run $4-$8. There is also lots of parking on residential lawns, cash only, usually running from $5-$10 all across the Big E area on adjacent streets. Be aware that parking in a non-parking area is strongly prohibited and police and tow companies are watching like hawks to make sure you follow the rules.

We hope that we were detailed enough in this post.  Thank You for reading.

# The Big E opens for 2025 season: What you need to know

by: Nick Antonakas

Posted: Sep 12, 2025 / 06:05 AM EDT

Updated: Sep 13, 2025 / 08:05 AM EDT

by: Nick Antonakas

Posted: Sep 12, 2025 / 06:05 AM EDT

Updated: Sep 13, 2025 / 08:05 AM EDT

SHARE – The Big E, the largest event on the East Coast and the fourth largest fair in North America, kicks off on Friday for a 17-day run.The fair opens with Military Appreciation Day, offering free admission to active duty, retired military personnel, and veterans with a valid ID. Last year, the fair set a new attendance record with over 1.63 million visitors, and the second weekend was particularly busy, with Saturday seeing nearly 180,000 attendees.

Visitors are advised to avoid traveling to the fair between 8:30 a.m. and 11 a.m. to avoid traffic congestion, and late-night departures are also busy.

## When do the buildings and Midway open?

   Big E gates open at 8:00 a.m.
   The Big E Bakery is open from 9:00 a.m. to 10:30 p.m.
   Buildings and Craft Common is open from 10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
   The Avenue of States and Storrowton Village Museum & Shops are open from 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
   The New England Center is open from 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
   Midway is open Sunday through Thursday from 11:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and Friday through Saturday at 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.

## When is my state/town day at The Big E?

Each day at the Big E honors something specific. For example, the first Friday is Military Appreciation Day at the Big E. Veterans, active duty military and their dependents all get in free. Here are all the special and state days this year:Friday, September 12 – Military Appreciation Day
   Saturday, September 13 – 4-H & FFA Day/Maine Day
   Sunday, September 14 – Storrowton Day
   Monday, September 15 – Salute to West Springfield
   Tuesday, September 16 – Rhode Island Day/Salute to Holyoke
   Wednesday, September 17 – Connecticut Day
   Thursday, September 18 – Massachusetts Day
   Friday, September 19 – New Hampshire Day
   Saturday, September 20 – Vermont Day
   Sunday, September 21 – Grange Day
   Monday, September 22 – Salute to Springfield
   Tuesday, September 23 – Salute to Chicopee
   Wednesday, September 24 – Salute to Agawam
   Thursday, September 25 – Salute to Westfield
   Friday, September 26 – Harvest New England Day
   Saturday, September 27 – Hooplandia Day
   Sunday, September 28 – Salute to Special Olympics

## Live Music at The Big E

This year’s music lineup for The Big E Arena and the Court of Honor stage has some iconic bands and musicians known across the country.

Here is who is playing at theCourt of Honorstage:(All concerts are free with fair admission)

   Tonic:September 12, 8:00 p.m.
   Jonathan Burns: September 12-17th, 12:00 p.m. or 5:00 p.m.
   The StepCrew: September 13-14th, 2:00 p.m.
   David Nihill: September 13, 8:00 p.m.
   Josh Morgan: September 14, 8:00 p.m.
   Augustana: September 14
   The Stylistics: September 15-16, 2:00 p.m.
   Al Jardine & The Pet Sounds Band: September 15-16, 8:00 p.m.
   The Marshall Tucker Band: September 17, 8:00 p.m.
   Gary Puckett & The Union Gap: September 17-18, 2:00 p.m.
   Aldo Nova:September 18, 8:00 p.m.
   B.o.B.:September 19, 8:00 p.m.
   Firefall: September 20, 8:00 p.m.
   Five for Fighting:September 21, 8:00 p.m.
   Seals & Crofts 2:September 22-23, 2:00 p.m.
   Sister Hazel:September 24, 8:00 p.m.
   Elliot Lurie of Looking Glass with Yacht Rock Gold Experience:September 25, 8:00 p.m.
   Finger Eleven:September 26, 8:00 p.m.
   MKTO:September 27, 8:00 p.m.
   Queensrÿche:September 28, 8:00 p.m.

Here is who is playing atThe Big E Arena: (all shows take place at 7:30 p.m.)

   Gov’t Mule: Back In The Saddle Tour with JJ Grey & Mofro: September 12th
   Busta Rhymes & Rick Ross: September 13th
   Cole Swindell with John Morgan: September 14th
   Collector Car Live with Ryan Preece: September 18th
   TLC with Big Boi: September 19th
   The Avett Brothers: September 20th
   Foreigner: September 21st
   The Kid LAROI:September 26th
   Train:September 27th
   ZZ Top: September 28th

## Admission Prices

The 2025 regular-price admission tickets are $20 for adults, $16 for seniors, and $12 for children ages 6 through 12, kids under 5 are free.

Presale tickets do offer a discount; however, all ticket sales are final. If you buy tickets in advance through September 10th, they are $17.50 for adults and $12 for children ages 6 through 12. If you plan to go to The Big E multiple times, there is a value pass option that gets you in daily during the 17 days of the fair for $71.50 per adult and $36.50 for children ages 6 through 12.

For $33.50, you can also get one wristband that includes unlimited rides at the Midway on the day you visit, Monday through Friday, or 78 credits on Saturday or Sunday.

Final preparations underway as the Big E set to open

## How much does parking cost?

If you plan to park on the Big E fairgrounds, all main parking will be found at Gate 9, which is the first gate on Memorial Avenue if you are coming from the east (from Springfield, Route 5, I-91, etc.) and the last gate if coming from the west (Agawam). It is cash-only parking, and there are no ATMs near the gate, so you will have to have $10 on hand to park. Motorcycles can park for $5 at Gate 9.

## About The Big E Fair

The 17-day long fair features hours of free entertainment and attractions, terrific food, authentic New Orleans Mardi Gras in The Big Parade, an immersive Ireland adventure in the International Plaza’s Dingle Peninsula Showcase, North American Midway, as well as educational opportunities from the Avenue of States to Storrowton Village Museum, Farm-A-Rama, and more.

## What time do the gates and buildings open?

   The gates open at 8:00 a.m. every day. 
   The Big E Bakery is open from 9:00 a.m. until 10:30 p.m.
   The Buildings and Craft Common is open from 10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
   The Avenue of States and Storrowton Village Museum & Shops is open from 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
   The New England Center is open from 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
   The Midway is open Sunday-Thursday, 11 a.m. – 10 p.m., and Friday-Saturday, 10 a.m. – 11 p.m.

## What is the cost of admission?

The Big E offers a full season pass that you could purchase, which costs $70 for adults, and for children ages 6-12 costs $35. If you purchase tickets at the gate, it costs $20 for adults, $12 for children 6-12, and admission is free for children five and under.

There are some days during the fair that offers discounted tickets. Opening day is Be A Kid For A Day, which means that admission costs $12 for everyone. Military Appreciation Day is also opening day, and free admission is provided with a veteran or military ID to:Active duty and retired military personnel
   Dependents of active duty military personnel
   Veterans (no dependents)

There is also Eleven-After-Five, which means that tickets cost $11 after 5:00 p.m. Sunday through Thursday.

Senior Days are Sunday through Thursday and tickets will cost $16 for anyone 60 years old and over.

## How much does parking cost?

There is on-site parking that is available for $10 (cash only) in Lot 9.Motorcycles can park in Lot 9 for $5 (cash only), and bicycles and bird scooters can park for free at 915 Memorial Avenue.

The Gate 9A area is available for drop-off/pick-up of passengers and has a large canvas tent with benches.

## Is there handicapped parking?

The Big E provides 580 handicapped accessible parking spaces on a first-come, first-served basis.

# The Big E: 2025 Information

The 2025 Big E will take place from Friday, September 12 through Sunday, September 28 at the...

The 2025 Big E will take place from Friday, September 12 through Sunday, September 28 at the Eastern States Exposition fairgrounds in West Springfield(Western Mass News)

By Western Mass News staff

Published: Sep. 4, 2024 at 12:49 PM EDT|Updated: Sep. 2, 2025 at 3:55 PM EDT

Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google

>>> >>>

(WGGB/WSHM) -- The 2025 Big E will take place from Friday, September 12 through Sunday, September 28 at the Eastern States Exposition fairgrounds in West Springfield. As you and your family prepare to take in the food and fun at this year’s fair, here’s some helpful information:

  
    

## TICKETS

Tickets are needed to enter the fair and can be purchased online or in-person at the fairgrounds during regular fair hours. Note: ticketed concerts at The Big E include fair admission.

   

## HOURS

- Gates: 8 a.m.
- The Big E Bakery: 9 a.m. to 10:30 p.m.
- Buildings and Craft Common: 10 a.m. to 10 p.m.
- Avenue of States and Storrowton Village Museum and Shops: 10 a.m. to 9 p.m.
- New England Center: 10 a.m. to 9 p.m.
- Midway: Sunday-Thursday, 11 a.m. to 10 p.m.; Friday-Saturday, 10 a.m. to 11 p.m.
   

## PARKING

  
VEHICLES: On-site parking is available for $10 (cash only) for cars and trucks. Motorcycles can park for $5 (cash only). Parking will be accessible via Gate 9. Fair officials said that 580 handicapped accessible parking spaces will be available at Gate 9 on a first-come, first-serve basis.   
BICYCLES: Free parking is available at 915 Memorial Avenue.   
    

## FAIR MAP

CLICK HERE for a printable map of the fairgrounds

  
    

## STATE AND SPECIAL DAYS
